positions.title: BIS Intern (Software Developer Intern)
positions.description:
•	Assisted in developing enterprise-level software applications and programs with the incorporation of SAFE Agile methodologies for software development to ensure timely delivery of requirements.
•	Developed logic with ASP .Net, C# .Net, and SQL Server to support development, testing, and production support activities.
•	Created N-tier architecture financial planning software using object-oriented programming concepts and test-driven development strategies.
•	Built Rest API controllers and web services client classes to interact with downstream systems and implementing Web API with JSON Web Tokens to secure the Web API Service Layer.

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description:
Social Media Data Analysis for Ride-Hailing Service Assessment.
Worked Under Dr. Kim and graduate student Ms. Anna Philips on transportation assessment to analyze public reviews on social media regarding public transportation companies like Uber and Lyft.
Used various approaches of AI like machine learning algorithms and natural language processing to process complicated data set to identify some patterns like user’s perception and sentiments.
In specific used CNN (convolutional neural network), Support Vector Machine, and other AI algorithms for natural language processing and compared the efficiency and run time of different AI frameworks with the proposed framework.

company.name: The University of Texas at Arlington

positions.title: Teaching Assistant (Peer Educator)
positions.description:
Helped the math and computer science department at UTA in decreasing the drop rate of the basic math courses like Precalculus, calculus1, and calculus, and helping students with C++, C.
Responsible for leading group sessions and individual sessions to teach C++, C and calculus and do the exam reviews for more than 25 students in a session.
Assisted professors in building strategies and in modifying class curriculum to improve student's understanding of concepts in the class.
With the purpose of being as helpful and available as possible, in order for students to succeed in the course.
